prompt_en: A fictional clinical encounter charged with dread, photographed as a grounded hospital scene. The central figure is a reference-inspired woman, preserving the supplied portrait's facial appearance and short dark bob with a light, separated fringe. She stands at the after-hours discharge records counter in a charcoal sleeveless jersey top and pale trousers, wearing a narrow hospital identification band. She has just been handed an empty transparent record sleeve. Her left hand pinches the open top of the empty sleeve while its lower edge rests on the patient-side counter; the fingers of her right hand remain on the metal lip of the now-closed transfer hatch. Through the clear lower portion of the security glass, her thick chart stands tilted on a document rest on the staff side, its outer folder facing the glass, close enough to see yet physically beyond her reach. The small portrait clipped to that chart repeats her face. Her eyes are fixed on this inaccessible file, her lips slightly parted and her shoulders held still; a soft amber desk lamp catches her cheek and bare forearm, giving her an intimate human presence against the building's indifferent surfaces. Immediately beyond her, a closed hospital exit door in the near background has a plainly visible steel sliding bolt crossing the door seam, with its two fixed endpoints visible. The waiting seats are empty, a queue dispenser hangs idle, and the long corridor of numbered clinical doors leads into fluorescent distance. The viewer stands diagonally along the patient side of the counter at her eye level, seeing her face in three-quarter view, close enough to understand the empty sleeve and her interrupted gesture while keeping the chart, glass barrier, and bolted exit legible in the same horizontal 3:2 environmental medium frame. Keep enough depth of field to distinguish the closed hatch and the nearby door bolt as actual separate boundaries. Restrained color photography, cool green-white institutional light, one small amber pool, mild grain, real worn laminate and rubbed stainless steel. The frightening event is the hospital retaining control of her record after the ordinary promise of discharge; her living, particular presence meets a system that has stopped responding.
